message:
fix(host): stop charging a window for a refusal that was ours

Product 2, test 1. The reviewer found this one and it is a real defect.

thumb_busy and thumb_helper_lingering came back as Failed, and the control session records that
against the window -- spending one of its three attempts. Neither has anything to do with the
window. One means another dispatcher was already in a capture; the other means a previous helper
will not die. Three of those and a window that has done nothing wrong sits out a sixty second
cooldown, and with two dispatchers three is not a lot.

They are Canceled now, which is the outcome that already means "nothing was asked of it" and which
the budget treats as free. That distinction existed and these two paths were on the wrong side of
it.

The race check now asserts the outcome and not just the detail string, so a refusal going back to
Failed fails a test rather than quietly costing windows their retries.

Two stale comments found in the same pass. killConfirmed said it was "read by the caller after
teardown" and no caller reads it. And host_control_session still described the concurrency bound as
structural and unenforced, which was true when it was written and stopped being true when the
helper started enforcing a cap of one -- the definition was corrected earlier and the use site was
not.

One correction to something I reported: I said the kill confirmation costs about 166ms. That was
inferred by subtracting a 400ms deadline from a 566ms total, which also contains the spawn. The
reviewer's instrumented measurement puts teardown at 8-60ms, and that number supersedes mine --
it was measured where mine was arithmetic.

The new assertion has not been run. It needs the helper end-to-end suite, which starts capture
processes, and that is paused. Budget 45, wait 20, fetch policy 13 and the shipped helper gate 16
all still pass, and none of them touch this path.
